Russian president describes Ukrainian counterpart’s letter as rude and says he sees no point in face-to-face talks Vladimir Putin has rejected an offer from Volodymyr Zelenskyy to hold a face-to-face meeting, insisting instead that Russia will achieve its war goals in Ukraine, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region. Speaking at the St Petersburg economic forum, the Russian president described the open letter from his Ukrainian counterpart containing the offer as rude. He refused to use Zelenskyy’s name, referring to him only as its author. Asked if they could meet to discuss an end to the conflict, Putin replied: “So far I see no point.”

Zelenskyy’s letter, which was published on Thursday, proposed a meeting in a third country such as Switzerland or Turkey. It said diplomacy should start from the current frontline and that Ukraine was ready for a full ceasefire while negotiations took place. The letter also alluded to Russia’s recent military setbacks and the growing fuel shortages in Crimea caused by Ukrainian attacks on crucial supply routes. Hours before the forum opened on Wednesday, Ukrainian drones hit St Petersburg’s oil terminal, sending black smoke billowing into the sky. Putin shrugged off the embarrassing strikes on his home city and said his territorial demands were unchanged. He said Russia controlled all of the Luhansk region – a claim Kyiv denies – and more than 85% of Donetsk region. He repeated his demand that Ukraine also give up all of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions.

Calling for “long-term peace”, he asked: “What is this letter about? Is it a means to create an environment for a personal meeting? Or is it meant to make sure no personal meeting takes place. I think it’s the second.” Speaking to Russian troops, he said: “Keep working, brothers”. Zelenskyy said Putin’s rejection showed the Kremlin had no wish to end the conflict. “Unfortunately, the Russian side is once again choosing war. Everyone heard the response. A weak response,” he said in his nightly video address. “I think this response will have disappointed many in the world.”

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Russian president describes Ukrainian counterpart’s letter as rude and says he sees no point in face-to-face talks

Vladimir Putin has rejected an offer from Volodymyr Zelenskyy to hold a face-to-face meeting, insisting instead that Russia will achieve its war goals in Ukraine, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region.

Speaking at the St Petersburg economic forum, the Russian president described the open letter from his Ukrainian counterpart containing the offer as rude. He refused to use Zelenskyy’s name, referring to him only as its author. Asked if they could meet to discuss an end to the conflict, Putin replied: “So far I see no point.”

Zelenskyy’s letter, which was published on Thursday, proposed a meeting in a third country such as Switzerland or Turkey. It said diplomacy should start from the current frontline and that Ukraine was ready for a full ceasefire while negotiations took place.

The letter also alluded to Russia’s recent military setbacks and the growing fuel shortages in Crimea caused by Ukrainian attacks on crucial supply routes. Hours before the forum opened on Wednesday, Ukrainian drones hit St Petersburg’s oil terminal, sending black smoke billowing into the sky.

Putin shrugged off the embarrassing strikes on his home city and said his territorial demands were unchanged. He said Russia controlled all of the Luhansk region – a claim Kyiv denies – and more than 85% of Donetsk region. He repeated his demand that Ukraine also give up all of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions.

Calling for “long-term peace”, he asked: “What is this letter about? Is it a means to create an environment for a personal meeting? Or is it meant to make sure no personal meeting takes place. I think it’s the second.” Speaking to Russian troops, he said: “Keep working, brothers”.

Zelenskyy said Putin’s rejection showed the Kremlin had no wish to end the conflict. “Unfortunately, the Russian side is once again choosing war. Everyone heard the response. A weak response,” he said in his nightly video address. “I think this response will have disappointed many in the world.”

Putin acknowledged Russia needed to strengthen its air defences but played down Ukraine’s increasingly successful campaign against strategic targets. Ukrainian drones hit five Russian cargo ships in the occupied southern ports of Mariupol and Berdiansk, and in the Sea of Azov, overnight on Thursday.

payload.title: Putin torjui Zelenskyin tapaamistarjouksen ja piti kiinni Venäjän sotatavoitteista
payload.summary: Vladimir Putin sanoi Pietarin talousfoorumissa, ettei näe toistaiseksi syytä kasvokkaiselle tapaamiselle Volodymyr Zelenskyin kanssa. Zelenskyi oli ehdottanut neuvotteluja kolmannessa maassa ja täyttä tulitaukoa niiden ajaksi.
payload.content:
Vladimir Putin on torjunut Volodymyr Zelenskyin ehdotuksen suorasta tapaamisesta ja vakuuttanut, että Venäjä aikoo saavuttaa sotatavoitteensa Ukrainassa. Pietarin talousfoorumissa puhunut Venäjän presidentti kuvaili Zelenskyin avointa kirjettä töykeäksi ja sanoi, ettei näe toistaiseksi järkeä kasvokkaisissa neuvotteluissa sodan päättämisestä.

## Zelenskyi ehdotti tapaamista kolmannessa maassa

Zelenskyin torstaina julkaistu kirje ehdotti tapaamista kolmannessa maassa, esimerkiksi Sveitsissä tai Turkissa. Kirjeen mukaan diplomatian pitäisi lähteä nykyisestä rintamalinjasta, ja Ukraina olisi valmis täyteen tulitaukoon neuvottelujen ajaksi.

Putin ei käyttänyt Zelenskyin nimeä, vaan viittasi häneen kirjeen kirjoittajana. Kun Putinilta kysyttiin, voisivatko johtajat tavata keskustellakseen konfliktin lopettamisesta, hän vastasi, ettei näe siinä toistaiseksi järkeä. Hän myös arvioi, että kirjeen tarkoitus saattoi olla pikemminkin estää henkilökohtainen tapaaminen kuin luoda sille edellytyksiä.

## Aluevaatimukset pysyivät ennallaan

Putin sanoi Venäjän vaatimusten pysyvän muuttumattomina. Hän toisti tavoitteensa koko itäisen Donbasin haltuun ottamisesta ja vaati Ukrainaa luopumaan myös Hersonin ja Zaporizhzhian alueista. Putinin mukaan Venäjä hallitsee koko Luhanskin aluetta, minkä Kiova kiistää, sekä yli 85 prosenttia Donetskin alueesta.

Zelenskyin kirje viittasi myös Venäjän viimeaikaisiin sotilaallisiin takaiskuihin ja Krimin kasvaviin polttoainepuloihin, joiden kerrottiin johtuvan Ukrainan iskuista tärkeille huoltoreiteille. Tunteja ennen foorumin avautumista keskiviikkona ukrainalaiset droonit iskivät Pietarin öljyterminaaliin, josta nousi mustaa savua taivaalle. Putin vähätteli iskuja kotikaupunkiinsa ja kehotti venäläisjoukkoja jatkamaan toimintaansa.

## Zelenskyi syytti Kremliä sodan valitsemisesta

Zelenskyi sanoi iltapuheessaan, että Putinin torjunta osoittaa Kremlin olevan haluton lopettamaan konfliktia. Hänen mukaansa Venäjän puoli valitsee jälleen sodan, ja Putinin vastaus oli heikko. Zelenskyi arvioi, että vastaus tuottaisi pettymyksen monille maailmassa.
